page: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor providing 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at a rated clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 KB of L1d cache, supplemented by hardware acceleration features such as AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for tile and int8 operations, and vector AES cryptography. System memory totals 512.0 GB, maintaining an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Attached storage consists of a bundled 3,780 GB NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute and memory bandwidth throughput across parallelized workloads. The multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 338.7 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems, alongside high scores in Geekbench multi-core (16,820.0), clang compilation (44,357.0), and PassMark CPU score (72,789.57). Cached memory read bandwidth peaks at 4,509.39 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads reach 246.15 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core benchmarks remain near median levels, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1,718.29 and Geekbench single-core score of 1,665.0. Write memory bandwidth across large blocks is average at 83.45 GB/sec.

The combination of Intel AMX extensions, 512 GB of memory, and fast read memory bandwidth translates to strong performance in data-intensive and in-memory contexts. Redis SET benchmarks reach 84.54 million operations per second, static web serving throughput measures 79.93 GB/sec, and database operations score 28,978.89 in PassMark. LLM prompt processing registers in the top tier across model tiers, processing 2,899.43 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models and 37.32 tokens/sec on 70B parameter models. Text generation for 70B parameter models drops to an average rate of 4.17 tokens/sec due to memory write limits and the absence of discrete accelerators.

From a resource and density perspective, the E64ds_v6 delivers strong cost efficiency for high-capacity memory footprints that also require substantial local temporary storage. Workload profiles best suited to this architecture include in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching tiers, Clang-based compilation pipelines, relational database management systems needing high IOPS local scratch space, and CPU-driven machine learning inference pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v6 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, it offers 512.0 GB of system RAM, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core, and integrates a 3,780 GB local NVMe SSD. Advanced hardware instructions include AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions, supporting elevated performance in parallel tasks. Benchmarks place this instance in the top tier for multi-core compute, cached read memory bandwidth at 4,509.39 GB/sec, Clang compilation, and in-memory operations, where it achieves 84.54 million Redis SET operations per second. With zero dedicated GPUs, single-thread metrics remain average. This hardware configuration is well matched for memory-heavy enterprise databases, large Redis clusters, high-throughput web serving, and CPU-based vector inference.
